propositions: The jira_dc_pat fixture is function-scoped, so each test mints a new Personal Access Token and never deletes it, exhausting Jira DC's 10-PAT-per-user cap.
PAT creation fails with a 403 UserTokenLimitExceededException, killing the live harness at setup and blocking all live acceptance evidence.
The failure mis-attributes to an unrelated module (test_transport.py) because the cause is the session-wide PAT budget, not the test that surfaces the error.
The failure looks flaky but is deterministic: tokens self-clear after a day via expirationDuration=1, so whether a run fails depends on recent instance usage and test count.
Making jira_dc_pat session-scoped turns PAT consumption from O(tests) into O(1), giving structural headroom as more live tests are added.
A session-start sweep should delete leftover rebar-j5-harness-* tokens from crashed runs while degrading safely and never deleting unrelated PATs.
